title: Speculative tile fusion race leads to KV-stripe aliasing and small softmax bias
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: We observed a low-frequency correctness regression in generation outputs after enabling an experimental speculative tile-fusion path combined with a new affine memory interleaving optimization for KV slabs. Under a tight prefill->decode scheduling window and backpressure from the coalescer, decoder workers can transiently take ownership of a KV slab slice that is still being compacted by the prefill path. The result is a brief aliasing of adjacent KV stripes and a small but measurable softmax probability bias (typically ~1e-5 to 1e-3 on affected tokens) that accumulates across long generations. This ticket tracks root cause, mitigations, and rollout gating for the fusion/interleaving feature set.
repro_steps: 1) Start a multi-stream prefill workload with batch size distribution skewed to large prefill requests (see workload fixture prefill-heavy-24.json),
3) Run generation on a long-context LLM (sequence length >= 2048) and sample with temperature 0.7 for 1000 tokens,

4) Compare token probability traces across baseline and experimental runtime using the probability-diff harness (link below). The failure is intermittent (~0.5%-2% of runs) and more likely under contention and mixed-precision (fp16) workloads.
investigation_notes: Observed pattern: numeric deltas are concentrated immediately after a prefill boundary where the decoder resumes with a speculative fused kernel. The KV indices pointed to adjacent slab offsets in a small fraction of runs.
Heap traces show two owners for same slab range for ~150-600us in failing traces; ownership handoff not synchronized by existing handshake when speculative fusion bypasses the usual prefetch path.
Reproducer harness written (tools/tests/kv_alias_repro.py). Repro rate ~1.4% on local 8-GPU perf cluster, ~0.6% on CI with synthetic contention.

Numeric analysis: typical softmax downstream bias manifests as probability mass shift yielding different top-1 token in 0.08% of tokens on failing runs; cumulatively visible on long sampled generations.
Attempted quick fix: added an extra atomic fence in ownership transition; reduced repro rate to ~0.2% but introduced ~1.6% latency p90 regressions for small batches due to additional contention.
short_term_mitigation: Gate the spec-tile-fusion flag behind staged rollout: disable by default for mixed-precision fp16 path and add runtime knob to force strict ownership handshake (--force-kv-handshake). Roll back affine interleaving to interleave=1 in release branches until fix is merged.
long_term_plan: 1) Implement explicit ownership handshakes between prefill and decode when speculative fusion is enabled; handshake must be lock-free and bounded (proposal in doc/kv-handshake-proposal.md).
2) Replace ad-hoc atomic fence with epoched slab allocator: epoch increments on compaction, decoder checks epoch snapshot vs slab epoch to detect alias window without heavy locking.
3) Add deterministic integration test in CI that reproduces alias condition at higher probability by manipulating timing (test harness will inject scheduler yield points).
4) Performance verification: run perf matrix (batch sizes, sequence lengths, fp16/fp32, interleave values) and compare p50/p90 token-host latency and repro-rate.
acceptance_criteria: Fix merged that removes ownership races (no dual-owner window observable in trace logs),
Regression harness shows repro rate < 0.01% across perf-cluster with spec-tile-fusion enabled,
End-to-end e2e sampling quality metrics show no statistically significant softmax drift vs baseline (A/B test),
Documentation updated and feature gate/flags adjusted for safe rollout.
